picks.title: Nuance of Wonder: Joan Tollifson
picks.summary:
Joan Tollifson returns to the podcast three years after her first conversation. We talk about her June essay Two Inseparable Truths, on the relative and the absolute and the trouble with getting stuck in either one. Along the way: the silence of many nondual teachers in a dark time, what cancer and an aging body insist on that philosophy cannot, why she has never used AI, and why "I don't know" may be the answer closest to true. She closes by reading her essay Radiant Light in Dark Times in full.

picks.reason: Discusses nondual Buddhist philosophy and facing uncertainty and impermanence.

picks.title: Grace in Prison
picks.summary:
In this Wednesday Night Dharma Talk, Sensei Dainin describes bringing Roshi Joan’s G.R.A.C.E. compassion training into New Mexico’s prison system. Working previously with the correctional cadets, and now with men who are incarcerated, Dainin names how the system pushes both groups into opposition, each side dehumanizing the other by default. Looking for guidance on how to serve well in that…
Source
picks.reason: A Zen teacher applies compassion training in prison, addressing suffering and ethical service.
